import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 34

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
-/

namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture34

open SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]

-- TODO: this statement is tagged `solved` but does not record the answer; determine it and
-- replace `answer(sorry)` with `answer(True)` or `answer(False)`.
set_option linter.style.category_answer false in
/--
WOWII [Conjecture 34](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph `G`, `path(G) ≥ ⌈dist_avg(C, V) + dist_avg(M, V)⌉`,
where `path(G)` is the floor of the average distance of `G`, `C` is the set of center
vertices (those with minimum eccentricity), `M` is the set of maximum-degree vertices,
and `dist_avg(S, V)` is the average distance from all vertices to the set `S`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem conjecture34 :
  answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (α : Type) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]
      (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h : G.Connected),
      let C : Set α := center G
      let M : Set α := {v | G.degree v = G.maxDegree}
      Int.ceil (distavg G C + distavg G M) ≤ (path G : ℤ) := by
  sorry

-- Sanity checks

/-- The `path G` invariant is nonneg when cast to ℤ. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) : 0 ≤ (path G : ℤ) := Int.natCast_nonneg _

/-- The edgeless graph on 3 vertices has no edges. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example : (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)).edgeFinset.card = 0 := by decide +native

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture34

findings.description: Both occurrences of `distavg` use the wrong averaging operation. `SimpleGraph.distavg G S` is (1/|V|) ∑v min_{s∈S} d(v,s), including the zero contributions from vertices in S. The source instead averages all nonzero pairwise distances d(s,v), with s∈S and v∈V; for the permitted connected graphs its denominator is |S|(|V|−1). Thus both taking minima and including zeros change the claim. This is not an equivalent reformulation: a 39-vertex tree consisting of a hub with three pendant leaves and a five-edge stem to the root of a full binary tree of depth four has path number 11. Its center and maximum-degree sets are singletons, with distance sums 154 and 266. Lean's bound is ceil(420/39)=11, whereas the source's bound is ceil(420/38)=12. `/workspace/review/witness.lean` proves that the existing per-graph assertion holds and the source assertion fails.
findings.source_evidence: WOWII all.html, Conjecture 34, states `path(G) ≥ CEIL[dist_avg(C,V) + dist_avg(M,V)]`. Its linked definitions 37 and 38 in wowIIdefs.js define these quantities as the average of all nonzero d_G(u,v) with u in M or C, respectively, and v in V. Read at https://web.archive.org/web/20260726061534id_/http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html and https://web.archive.org/web/20260723211215id_/http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/wowIIdefs.js .
findings.suggested_fix: Introduce a separate pair-distance average: let `pairs := (S.toFinset ×ˢ Finset.univ).filter (fun p => 0 < G.dist p.1 p.2)` and return `(∑ p ∈ pairs, (G.dist p.1 p.2 : ℝ)) / (pairs.card : ℝ)`. Use it for both C and M, and update the averaging description in the docstring. Under the existing hypotheses this is equivalently the double distance sum divided by |S|(|V|−1). Do not retain the nearest-set minimum.

findings.description: The docstring says `path(G)` is the floor of the average distance. The imported `SimpleGraph.path` actually counts vertices in a largest induced path, which is the source's intended invariant. Only this part of the prose is wrong; the current `path` definition should not be changed. Lean checks give path(K₂)=2 but floor(averageDistance(K₂))=1.
findings.source_evidence: Definition 35 in the source's wowIIdefs.js says: “path number of a graph … The number of vertices of a largest induced path of the graph.” https://web.archive.org/web/20260723211215id_/http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/wowIIdefs.js .
findings.suggested_fix: Replace “the floor of the average distance of G” with “the number of vertices of a largest induced path of G.”

trivial_proof.lean:
import FormalConjectures.WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture34

/-! A concrete check of the distance averages used in WOWII Conjecture 34. -/

local notation "K₂" => (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2))

-- WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture34.conjecture34:
-- On K₂, both averages used by the theorem are 0, whereas the source's
-- average of all nonzero pair distances is (1 + 1) / 2 = 1 for each set.
-- Source: wowIIdefs.js, definitions 37 and 38; both sets here are all vertices.
example : SimpleGraph.Connected K₂ ∧
    SimpleGraph.distavg K₂ (SimpleGraph.center K₂) = 0 ∧
    SimpleGraph.distavg K₂
      {v | SimpleGraph.degree K₂ v = SimpleGraph.maxDegree K₂} = 0 ∧
    ((SimpleGraph.dist K₂ 0 1 : ℝ) + (SimpleGraph.dist K₂ 1 0 : ℝ)) / 2 = 1 := by
  have hM : {v : Fin 2 | SimpleGraph.degree K₂ v = SimpleGraph.maxDegree K₂} =
      Set.univ := by ext v; fin_cases v <;> decide
  have hV : (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin 2)) = {0, 1} := by decide
  norm_num [SimpleGraph.center_top, hM, SimpleGraph.distavg, SimpleGraph.distToSet,
    SimpleGraph.dist_top, hV]

submission.summary: Replaced both nearest-set averages with a local average over all nonzero vertex-pair distances. Corrected the docstring, recorded answer(False), and documented the checked 39-vertex counterexample while retaining the solved category. Only the requested file was edited; it compiles with no warnings other than the permitted sorry warning.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 34

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
-/

namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture34

open SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 34](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph `G`, `path(G) ≥ ⌈dist_avg(C, V) + dist_avg(M, V)⌉`,
where `path(G)` is the number of vertices of a largest induced path of `G`, `C` is
its set of center vertices (those with minimum eccentricity), `M` is its set of
maximum-degree vertices, and `dist_avg(S, V)` is the average of all nonzero distances
`dist_G(s, v)` over pairs with `s ∈ S` and `v ∈ V`.

The conjecture is false. Take a vertex with three pendant leaves and a five-edge path
from it to the root of a perfect binary tree of depth four. This tree has 39 vertices
and path number 11. Its center and maximum-degree sets are singletons with total
distances 154 and 266, respectively, so the proposed bound is `⌈(154 + 266) / 38⌉ = 12`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem conjecture34 :
  answer(False) ↔
    ∀ (α : Type) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]
      (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h : G.Connected),
      let C : Set α := center G
      let M : Set α := {v | G.degree v = G.maxDegree}
      let distAvgFrom (S : Set α) : ℝ :=
        open scoped Classical in
        let pairs := (S.toFinset ×ˢ Finset.univ).filter (fun p => 0 < G.dist p.1 p.2)
        (∑ p ∈ pairs, (G.dist p.1 p.2 : ℝ)) / (pairs.card : ℝ)
      Int.ceil (distAvgFrom C + distAvgFrom M) ≤ (path G : ℤ) := by
  sorry

-- Sanity checks

/-- The `path G` invariant is nonneg when cast to ℤ. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) : 0 ≤ (path G : ℤ) := Int.natCast_nonneg _

/-- The edgeless graph on 3 vertices has no edges. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example : (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)).edgeFinset.card = 0 := by decide +native

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture34
